rows.grounds: optative verb expressing injunction to mutter or recite
demonstrative pronoun referring to the practitioner
optative verb indicating the resulting state
adverb qualifying the speed of attainment
genitive object of vallabhaḥ; vidyā may denote mantra-knowledge or its presiding power
predicate noun describing the practitioner's relation to the vidyā
emphasizes attainment occurring of its own accord

items.question: What attainment in relation to the vidyā follows from reciting this practice?
premises: The practitioner should recite the prescribed practice.
Recitation results in becoming beloved of the vidyā.
This attainment occurs quickly and of itself.
items.inference: Therefore, one who recites this practice swiftly becomes the beloved of the vidyā.
uncertainties: vidyāyāḥ may refer specifically to mantra-knowledge, a deity, or a form of sacred knowledge.
items.plain_english: He should recite it; he will quickly become the beloved of the vidyā himself.
